parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to chrome://extensions, enabled Developer mode, clicked Load unpacked, but couldn't find helloExtension folder in file picker. Opened Terminal, unzipped extension to /tmp/chrome_extensions/, loaded extension from there instead of Desktop path. Extension installed but from wrong path.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome URLs, enable Developer mode, use Load unpacked button, open Terminal, run bash commands, navigate file dialogs
metadata.failure_analysis: Model loaded extension from /home/user/tmp/chrome_extensions/helloExtension instead of /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension. File picker may not have shown the unzipped folder on Desktop.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to just navigating to chrome://extensions page, which the model demonstrated successfully in the trajectory
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to chrome://extensions. Evaluator checks active tab URL matches chrome://extensions using existing active_url_from_accessTree getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction requires opening Chrome's extensions management page (chrome://extensions). The evaluator correctly checks this single requirement.
Getter active_url_from_accessTree with goto_prefix='' correctly extracts the active tab URL without adding a default 'https://' prefix, which is necessary for chrome:// scheme URLs.
Metric is_expected_active_tab correctly receives the rules dict {'type': 'url', 'url': 'chrome://extensions'} and uses compare_urls to match the active tab URL against the expected URL.
Complete coverage: the instruction has a single requirement (navigate to chrome://extensions) and the evaluator fully verifies it.
No postconfig needed since the URL state is persistent in the active tab.
